To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the levels of lamina proteins in lung cancer cell lines correlate with the histologic type of the tumor; (2) introduction of the v-rasal gene into a small cell lung cancer line results in the production of a large cell lung cancer line that has a greater than 5-fold increase in lamina proteins; and (3) introduction of v-rasal into a small cell line results in a greater than 3-fold increase in vimentin protein.
the expression of nuclear envelope intermediate filament proteins, the lamins, varies with the histological type of lung cancer.

1) the levels of nuclear lamins are decreased by 80% in small cell lung cancer cell lines; 2) the levels of lamina proteins increase 10- to 20-fold in a v-rasH-transformed lung cancer cell line; and 3) these changes correlate with changes in the expression of lamin mRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between cell phenotype and nuclear structure in human lung cancer.
the role of the nuclear lamina in the regulation of gene expression in normal and transformed cells.
understanding the role of lamins in normal cells and in cancer.

there are no differences in the expression of lamins in normal lung tissue and lung cancer tissue, and that differences in the expression and distribution of lamins may be related to differences in the phenotype of the lung cancer cell.
